To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of TILs and PD-L1 in the TME are independent prognostic factors in many cancers.

1) the tumor microenvironment can be classified into 4 different categories (TILs+PD-L1-, TILs+PD- L1+, TILs-PD-L1-, and TILs-PDL1+) and that 2) this classification can be used to predict the efficacy of immunotherapy and to rationally design combination therapies.

we identified four different classes of tumor microenvironment (TMEs) based on T-cell infiltration and PD-L1 expression, and that the combination of immune checkpoint blockade and chemotherapy is more effective in tumors with high T-cell infiltration and low PD-L1 expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) The development and characterization of new cancer cell lines, (2) The study of tumor immunology, and (3) The development of novel cancer therapies.
the development of novel methods for the analysis of the tumor microenvironment and the identification of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
the study of the molecular basis of the immune response to cancer, and with the design and evaluation of new immunotherapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD-L1 expression in the absence of TILs is associated with a poor prognosis in many cancers and that the presence of both TILs and PD-L1 is associated with an excellent prognosis.
PD-L1 expression is associated with an immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment, but that it is not the only factor to be considered.
the tumor immune microenvironment is complex and heterogeneous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of T-cell infiltration is a key feature in the tumor immune microenvironment.
the immune microenvironment of cancer is complex and that a combination approach to therapy is likely to be needed to achieve the best results.

we have shown that the tumor microenvironment has four distinct immunotypes, which we have termed “immunoscore.” This immunoscore has been shown to have a prognostic value and may help guide the selection of the best immunotherapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PD-L1 expression and T-cell infiltration are two independent variables that can be used to classify tumors.
the presence of PD-L1 on tumor cells is a marker of an immunogenic microenvironment, which can be targeted by immune checkpoint inhibitors.
PD-L1 expression and the immune context in the tumor microenvironment are key factors in predicting the response to immunotherapy.
